statement: Ragusa (Dubrovnik) existed within the Byzantine sphere of influence as a duchy under the Theme of Dalmatia until the 12th century. Byzantine cultural influence is visible in Ragusa's Orthodox community and its Greek-influenced legal practices. When Venice gained Ragusa under the Treaty of Zadar (1204, confirmed 1205), Byzantine influence waned. The city's sophisticated diplomatic tradition — maintaining simultaneous relations with multiple great powers — developed partly from its Byzantine administrative heritage and its position as a crossroads between Latin and Orthodox worlds.
